sources.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
sources.evidence: July 9, 2026 general-availability announcement identifies Sol as the flagship tier of the GPT-5.6 family, with API, ChatGPT and Codex access, reasoning and programmatic tool calling.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Sol — API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh Markdown lists gpt-5.6-sol as its default and only listed snapshot, gpt-5.6 as a routing alias, 1,050,000 context, 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens; text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded July 9 card with August corrections. Its Sol-specific evaluations, training section and full-text structural-term review disclose no production total/active parameter count or architectural classification. Small-model training benchmarks do not describe Sol’s own size.

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: July 29 engineering article describes next-token forward passes, KV caching, partitioning work across sub-networks, and speculative decoding. Architecture/size experiments concern Sol’s smaller draft model, not the primary Sol network. It provides no total/active count or explicit Transformer/dense/MoE designation.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded September 3 card includes numerous exact GPT-5.6 Sol comparison columns and discusses training, monitorability and pretraining evaluations. No numerical production count or structural specification for Sol was found in the reviewed text and tables.

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-6 Astra System Card: GPT-6.1 Sol
sources.evidence: Downloaded September 29 addendum compares exact GPT-5.6 Sol in safety, biological and cyber tables. These are evaluation scores, not model sizes. No production total/active count or architecture for GPT-5.6 Sol was found.

sources.title: File inputs — OpenAI API
sources.evidence: Responses accepts input_file; vision-capable models receive extracted PDF text and page images. Chat Completions accepts PDF file parts. Together with the exact Sol endpoint/vision listing, this supports PDF as an API input format.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2, 3.3 and 9.1 grant limited access to the hosted service, restrict reverse engineering and reserve OpenAI’s rights. Supports a descriptive Proprietary classification for the documented hosted model, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
sources.evidence: June 26 announcement describes a limited API/Codex preview restricted to a small group of trusted partners, with broader availability still planned. Distinguishes the preview from the July 9 public launch. The indexed primary page was readable; direct HTTP retrieval returned 403.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: July 9 explicitly releases gpt-5.6-sol and the gpt-5.6 alias. August 6 updates chat-latest while recommending production Sol separately; August 13 calls Ultrafast a service tier, not a new checkpoint.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes
sources.evidence: August 6 describes an updated Sol in the ChatGPT chat experience and explicitly excludes Work/Codex from that change. This does not establish a replacement of the gpt-5.6-sol production API snapshot.

sources.title: Prompt caching — OpenAI API
sources.evidence: Current guide covers GPT-5.6 and later and explains reuse of intermediate KV states, but does not specify this model’s network architecture or counts.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived February 18 article explains Transformer attention but explicitly limits its applicability to models before GPT-5.6. It cannot establish GPT-5.6 Sol’s architecture.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Preview System Card
sources.evidence: Indexed June 26 primary card identifies Sol within the GPT-5.6 family and its restricted preview. Model Data and Training describes data sources and reasoning reinforcement learning, not production parameter counts or network structure.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes the model and its system card.

family.note: The generation is GPT-5.6; Sol is its capability tier. Corrects baseline gpt-sol.

release_date.note: Public/general API release. June 26 was a restricted trusted-partner preview, not the broad release; later ChatGPT and serving-tier changes do not change this date.

open_weights.note: The documented release is a hosted service under OpenAI terms; the reviewed release and model documentation provide no downloadable Sol weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model under OpenAI service terms; no open-weight license is documented.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count found in the original/preview cards, later exact-model comparison tables, engineering article, or targeted first-party training/interpretability searches. GPU hours, benchmark scores and draft-model experiments are not production model counts.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count disclosed in those sources. Neither a total count nor a dense/MoE assumption can supply it.

architecture.note: No sufficient exact-model structural evidence found. KV caching and next-token forward passes alone do not establish Transformer; sub-networks do not establish MoE. The named architecture experiments are for a separate draft model. The older Transformer caching article explicitly excludes GPT-5.6+.

context_window.note: Exact API documentation states total context 1,050,000, maximum input 922,000 and maximum output 128,000 tokens. Product chat limits are separate.

modalities.note: Text/image are native API inputs; PDF is a supported file format converted to text/page images. Image-generation tool access is not native image output. Audio/video endpoints are not supported.

reasoning.note: API supports reasoning tokens and effort none, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. An optional none setting does not negate reasoning support.

tool_call.note: Exact model lists function calling and Responses tools; launch changelog also documents programmatic tool calling.

description.value: GPT-5.6 model for reasoning, coding, research, and tool-based work.
description.note: Replaces promotional wording with supported uses without asserting benchmark superiority or undisclosed structure.

patch.notes: July 9, 2026 is the public API release; June 26 was a restricted partner preview. The gpt-5.6 alias routes to gpt-5.6-sol; documentation lists no dated Sol snapshot. Context is 1,050,000 tokens, with explicit limits of 922,000 input and 128,000 output. PDF input is API text/page-image extraction. The August 6 ChatGPT update and August 13 Ultrafast service-tier announcement do not identify a new production Sol API checkpoint. Total/active parameters and exact architecture remain unverified or undisclosed; draft-model architecture and sub-network terminology do not establish Sol’s network structure.

summary: Audited all 14 fields. Corrects family to gpt-5.6, supplies Proprietary license classification and a factual description, and replaces catalog provenance with primary sources. Confirms July 9 public release, documented context, text/image/PDF inputs, text output, reasoning and tool use. Preserves null counts and architecture after original/later-card and technical-source checks; distinguishes preview, API alias, ChatGPT update and serving tiers.
